Maia for Content calendar coordination

Show what is ready, blocked, or missing in the publishing plan.

All use cases ↗

Establish the calendar source

Start by telling Maia which calendar or export is authoritative, when it was captured, and what each status means. "Draft" may mean the writer has started in one team and that an editor can review in another. Include the expected stages, owners, channels, and publication dates.

If the calendar is incomplete, say so. Maia can help identify missing fields, but it should not fill an empty owner or date from a previous assignment.

Compare status with discussion

Ask Maia to match calendar entries with explicit updates in the editorial Slack channel. A useful readiness view shows the source and time of each status. When an owner says a draft is ready but the calendar still says outlining, Maia can present the conflict for confirmation.

Group the output by the decision the editor needs to make. Items ready for review belong together. Work blocked on an interview, design asset, or product check needs a named dependency. Unscheduled ideas can remain separate from committed pieces.

Make dependencies concrete

"Blocked" is useful only when the team knows what will unblock the work. Ask Maia to name the missing input, its expected owner, and the date needed to protect publication. If any part is unknown, it should become a question.

For an article waiting on a product screenshot, the output might ask the product marketer to confirm the final interface by Tuesday. It should not infer that design owns the task because design handled a similar image last month.

Run the planning conversation

Post the readiness view before the editorial meeting. Owners can correct statuses in the thread, and Maia can produce a shorter decision list for the meeting itself. The managing editor chooses what moves, what slips, and what leaves the calendar.

This workflow prepares drafts and coordination. It does not publish content or change live dates in a calendar unless the team has separately configured and approved that action.

Begin with one cycle

Use one week or one campaign rather than the entire content program. Confirm that titles match across the calendar and Slack discussion. Review every missing owner and dependency. Once the team trusts the conventions, schedule the readiness view before the regular planning meeting.

Questions from editorial teams

Can Maia update the calendar?

Start with a review based on a supplied export. Configure and verify any write access separately, with clear authority for changing dates and owners.

How does it handle a stale status?

The view can show the last update time and ask the owner to confirm. It should keep the item unresolved until someone does.

Can freelancers appear in the report?

Yes, when the supplied calendar includes them and the Slack audience may see the relevant details. Keep private contract or personnel information out of the shared view.
